analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date and one new section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' (head lines 4816-4826). The supplied units (head lines 3593-4073) are unchanged surrounding documentation, with no changed lines in that range per the file_changes ranges. It covers link/share probe histories, batch-invariant projections, served speed records, Qwen/GLM tensor-parallel details and the prefix-cache tiers.

The new section states that GPT-OSS plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound (via CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding), that prefill keeps MLX defaults, and that results do not depend on the partitioning. This is a performance and availability tuning description. It does not touch the plaintext boundaries, the sealed all-sum, the prefix-cache encryption or scoping (T-041), attestation, authorization or the coordinator contract. I found no new trust boundary, secret handling or data exposure. Any GPU/memory availability effect of larger command-buffer batches is not visible here, and no source code is supplied. The claims about the 100-op limit and result invariance are unverified documentation claims.

The unit text I reviewed does not mention the new section, so I could not check it against the surrounding text. The pre-existing T-041 acceptance notes (SEC-035) in the documented prefix-cache tiers are not new. I found no concrete regression and no threat-model gap caused by this PR. A reviewer of the code side, if included in another batch, should confirm that GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers is applied only to decode, so the GPU and memory limits are unchanged.
